claim.pdf_says: 11.9.6   DEFAULT ROUNDED clause  [printed at exactly the same weight and size as 11.9.5 ARITHMETIC clause; both are third-level subsections of 11.9 OPTIONS paragraph]
claim.markdown_says: ## 11.9.6 DEFAULT ROUNDED clause  (with '### 11.9.6.1 General', '### 11.9.6.2 General format', '### 11.9.6.3 General rules')   [its peer is transcribed one level deeper: '### 11.9.5 ARITHMETIC clause' at specs/ISO_COBOL.md:13175 with '#### 11.9.5.1 General format' at :13180]
claim.why_it_matters: Clause 11.9 is internally inconsistent: subsections 11.9.1-11.9.5 are children of '## 11.9 OPTIONS paragraph' but 11.9.6 is a sibling of it, so DEFAULT ROUNDED falls outside the OPTIONS paragraph in any depth-based outline while ARITHMETIC stays inside. verdict.reasoning:
REFUTED. Nothing is missing and no normative content differs; the claim is a markdown heading-depth artifact, and its stated evidence from the PDF does not exist.

(1) The heading is NOT missing. Rendered PDF page 303 (printed folio 273) shows '11.9.6 DEFAULT ROUNDED clause' followed by '11.9.6.1 General', '11.9.6.2 General format', '11.9.6.3 General rules'. The markdown carries all four verbatim with correct numbers and titles (specs/ISO_COBOL.md:13217, :13220, :13225, :13241), plus correct anchors (section-11-9-6, -1, -2, -3) that encode the hierarchy properly. The body content is faithful too: general rule 1) matches word-for-word, all eight rounding modes are present in the correct order inside the brace, and the figure note correctly records which words are underlined. The transcription even preserves the real asymmetry between the two clauses -- 11.9.5 has no '.0 General' subsection (PDF page 302 runs body text directly under the 11.9.5 heading) while 11.9.6 does have 11.9.6.1 General. The kind label 'missing-heading' is simply wrong for what was found.

(2) The claim's PDF evidence is vacuously true and therefore proves nothing. I extracted the actual font metadata: EVERY heading on both pages is Cambria,Bold at 11.67pt -- '11.9 OPTIONS paragraph', '11.9.1 General', '11.9.5 ARITHMETIC clause', '11.9.5.1 General format', '11.9.6 DEFAULT ROUNDED clause' and '11.9.6.1 General' alike. Left margins are uniform per page (all ten headings at x=63 on PDF index 301, all four at x=80 on index 302; the 63-vs-80 delta is mirrored even/odd page margins, not level indentation). So the printed standard supplies NO typographic level distinction whatsoever. Saying 11.9.6 is 'printed at exactly the same weight and size as 11.9.5' is equally true of 11.9 one level ABOVE it and 11.9.6.1 one level BELOW it. The PDF cannot be said to assert any markdown heading depth, so there is no PDF statement for the markdown to contradict. In this standard the dotted section number is the sole level indicator -- and it is preserved exactly.

(3) The 'internally inconsistent, two peers at different depths' framing misrepresents the markdown. 11.9.6 is not a lone anomaly: every clause from 11.9.6 through 11.9.11 sits at '##' (ENTRY-CONVENTION :13258, FLOAT-BINARY :13308, FLOAT-DECIMAL :13336, INITIALIZE :13393, INTERMEDIATE ROUNDING :13464). Within 11.9 the odd one out is arguably 11.9.5, the single clause at '###'. The same off-by-one pervades all of section 11 independently of this page: '## 11 Identification division' (:12754, a top-level clause at depth 2), '## 11.7.4 General rules' (:13070), '## 11.9.9.3 Syntax rules' (:13378), '## 11.9.10.1'-'.4' (:13396-:13428), '## 11.10.4 General rules' (:13583). Markdown '#' depth is systemically unreliable across this transcription; it is not a page-303 content defect.

(4) No meaning changes. A consumer that resolves sections by their printed number -- which is how the standard itself and every citation in this project refer to them ('per 11.9.6') -- gets the correct answer from the markdown. Only a tool inferring hierarchy purely from '#' counts while ignoring the numbers would be misled, and such a tool is already broken on this document at '## 11' long before it reaches 11.9.6. Per the rejection criteria this is formatting that does not alter content or meaning.

If normalizing markdown heading depth to dotted-number depth is desired, that is a legitimate whole-document mechanical cleanup (dozens of headings in section 11 alone, and '## 11' itself). It is not a page-303 PDF/markdown content discrepancy and should not be filed as one.
verdict.corrected_description: Not a content discrepancy. The 11.9.6 DEFAULT ROUNDED clause heading, its three subsections, and all of its normative text are present and faithful on page 303. The only real difference is markdown '#' nesting depth, which is document-wide and systemic rather than specific to this page: 11.9.6 through 11.9.11 are all transcribed at '##' (11.9.5 at '###' is the local outlier), and the same off-by-one appears at '## 11', '## 11.7.4', '## 11.9.9.3', '## 11.9.10.1-.4' and '## 11.10.4'. The claim's supporting evidence is invalid: the printed standard renders EVERY heading level in identical Cambria,Bold 11.67pt at an identical per-page left margin, so relative print weight and size carry no level information and the PDF makes no assertion about heading depth. The dotted section number -- the standard's only level indicator -- is preserved exactly in the markdown, along with correct 'section-11-9-6*' anchors. Reclassify as an optional whole-document heading-depth normalization, not a page-303 reconciliation defect.
